topic.title: Customizing the Translation Behavior
topic.shortdesc: An overview of the translation customization mechanisms and the kinds of guidance you can give the translation agent.

body.p: You can steer how the translation agent behaves for your project through two complementary mechanisms.

section.title: Per-Job Prompt vs. agent-instructions.md

ul.li:
The per-job prompt - Free-form instructions you type in the Instructions field of the New Translation dialog when you start a translation job. These instructions apply only to that one job. They are useful for a one-off request, such as asking the agent to retranslate a topic in a particular way.
Per-Job Prompt in the New Translation Dialog

agent-instructions.md - An optional file at .contentfusion/i18n/agent-instructions.md in your project's repository. When present, it applies to every translation job that has it in the workspace. This is where you put durable, project-wide guidance: terminology, a style guide, do-not-translate lists, and any other customization described in this section.

section.p: Use the per-job prompt for one-time requests and agent-instructions.md for anything you want to apply consistently across translation jobs.

section.title: Referencing Other Files
section.p: agent-instructions.md does not have to contain everything inline. You can move detailed guidance into separate files, such as a terminology list, a style guide, or a doctype configuration, and reference them from agent-instructions.md, telling the agent when each one is relevant. Refer to a file by a path relative to agent-instructions.md.

Splitting guidance this way is more than tidiness. It lets the agent load only what a given job needs instead of front-loading every instruction into every job, a form of progressive disclosure. For example, guidance on adding a newly translated publication to your multilingual book matters only when you first translate that publication, and instructions for translating SVG text are irrelevant to an incremental job that touches no SVG files. Keeping such guidance in referenced files, consulted only when relevant, keeps each job focused on the task at hand.

section.title: Common Use Cases
section.p: The following topics walk through specific customizations you can describe in agent-instructions.md:
The sections below cover shorter customizations you can add directly to agent-instructions.md.

section.title: Do-Not-Translate Lists
section.p: To keep specific strings in their original form (product names, code identifiers, or UI labels that ship untranslated), list them and instruct the agent to leave them unchanged wherever they appear, for example:

p.codeblock: Never translate the following strings; keep them exactly as written: Content Fusion, oXygen, WebHelp, DITA-OT.

section.title: Style Guide
section.p: To apply your house style, describe it in agent-instructions.md or reference a separate style-guide file. Cover the choices that matter for your content, for example tone and register, how to address the reader, and punctuation or formatting conventions per language:

p.codeblock: Use a formal register and address the reader with the formal second person. Follow the target language's standard quotation marks. Keep UI labels in sentence case.

section.title: Translating Text Inside SVG Graphics
section.p: By default, SVG images are treated as binary assets and copied into each target language unchanged, so the text they contain is not translated. If diagram labels or other text inside your SVG graphics need to be localized, you can instruct the agent in agent-instructions.md to also translate the text content of the SVG files referenced from your content, for example:

p.codeblock: Always translate the text inside referenced SVG images (for example the content of <text> and <tspan> elements), leaving all other SVG markup unchanged.
